--- title: "Retrieving a schema from a table in polars" subtitle: "collect_schema" author: '{{< var author >}}' date: '2025-07-18' date-format: iso toc: true toc-title: 'Sections' toc-location: right toc-depth: 3 categories: [100DaysOfPolars] --- In addition to showing column data types in the dataframe, Polars allows you to get a dictionary of data types where the key is the column name and the value is the data type. This is especially helpful when you're writing data to a database and want the schema to be maintained. Below is a dataframe with various data types. ::: {#395e2906 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

## Get data types as dictionary To get the data types as a dictionary, you can use the Polars method `collect_schema`. Here's how to do it: ::: {#01eb2366 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(df .collect_schema() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Schema({'date': Datetime(time_unit='us', time_zone=None), 'sku': String, 'quantity': Int64, 'unit price': Float64}) ``` ::: ::: ## Get names, keys from schema The schema dictionary has properties that you can access. For instance, if you only want the table column names from the schema, you can get them like this: ::: {#4d312f8b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} (df .collect_schema() .names() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['date', 'sku', 'quantity', 'unit price'] ``` ::: ::: Or, if you want the data types, you can get them like this: ::: {#dd7b0031 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} (df .collect_schema() .keys() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` odict_keys(['date', 'sku', 'quantity', 'unit price']) ``` ::: ::: My {{< var polars_course >}} is accepting enrollments.
